clue.text: Square in which a port authority confines extreme characters

indicators.note: confines means the port authority's letters are wrapped round the other piece

parts.note: the PLA is the Port of London Authority
A and Z are the characters at the two extremes of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A harbour board fences off its most outlandish types somewhere in a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: The PLA (Port of London Authority) holds AZ, the letters at either end of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish-style town square or open marketplace is called this, a synonym.

clue.text: Expert forced open container of deed

indicators.note: container of means the word for forced open holds the deed inside it

parts.note: prised means levered open
an act is a deed

explanation.surface: A specialist breaks open the box holding a legal document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deed' looks like a legal document stored in a box; 'container of' says the word for forced open holds the word for deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Skilled and experienced through long repetition, an adjective meaning proficient.

clue.text: A historian's jacket

definitions.meaning: Lord ..., Victorian historian famed for 'power tends to corrupt'
a padded jacket worn under medieval armour

explanation.surface: A coat belonging to a scholar of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Acton was a 19th-century historian; the word is also a quilted tunic worn beneath mail.

clue.text: Publicize skill in manufacturing gliders, perhaps

parts.note: to air a view is to make it public
craft is manual skill in making things

explanation.surface: Promote the workmanship involved in building sailplanes.
explanation.definitionFit: Gliders are one example of flying machines, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: An Estonian, perhaps, introducing another one in Maryland

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase locating the answer, a city found in that US state

parts.note: an Estonian is one example of a Balt, a native of the Baltic states
another one is 'one more', I (one) followed by MORE

explanation.surface: A visitor from Tallinn brings along a compatriot to the eastern United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another one' is read as 'one more', giving I then MORE; 'introducing' simply joins BALT to them. The definition is a locating phrase: the answer is a place in Maryland.
explanation.definitionFit: Baltimore is the largest city of that eastern US state, on Chesapeake Bay.

clue.text: Strikers are crazy!

definitions.meaning: implements for hitting a ball, as in cricket or baseball
slang for mad, from '... in the belfry'

explanation.surface: Workers walking out are mad!
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket and baseball implements for striking the ball; also slang for mad or eccentric.

clue.text: Dull talks? Cruel fabrication

indicators.note: fabrication means the letters are made up into something new

explanation.surface: Boring speeches, and a nasty lie at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabrication' rearranges TALKS and CRUEL together.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking sparkle or vitality, a synonym of flat and uninspired.

clue.text: Write and charge with a crime, say

indicators.note: say means the word for charging with a crime is spoken out loud

parts.note: to indict is to formally accuse of a crime

explanation.surface: Put pen to paper and accuse someone of an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: INDICT is pronounced 'in-dite', the silent C making it sound just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An old literary verb for composing or putting into words on paper.

clue.text: Accidentally learnt of deliveries — difficult to keep a note

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries bowled

indicators.note: to keep means the word for difficult holds the note inside

parts.note: hard means difficult
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Picked up word about the post, a problem when one must hold onto a memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests post; in cricket, an over is six balls bowled. HARD keeps E.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught words by chance without being the intended listener, as through a thin wall.

clue.text: Duck of a rosy colour that's turned up

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the two pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: red is a rosy colour
ie is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A pink-tinged duck that has come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reverses RED + IE to give EIDERS letters in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A large northern sea duck prized for its soft down, so a species of that bird.

clue.text: Circle in which Scott once moved

definitions.text: Circle in which Scott once moved

parts.words: Circle in which Scott once moved
parts.note: reads like a social set a person named Scott mixed in, but means the polar line of latitude near which the explorer travelled to the South Pole

explanation.surface: A society crowd that a man called Scott used to frequent.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Falcon Scott led the ill-fated 1910-13 expedition to the South Pole; 'circle' suggests a social set, but is a line of latitude.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar circle near which Captain Scott's southern expedition travelled is named after that frozen continent.

clue.text: Nymph has change of heart, revealing great fear

indicators.note: change of heart means the middle letter of the nymph's name is swapped for another

parts.note: a dryad is a tree nymph of Greek myth

explanation.surface: A woodland spirit changes her mind and shows she is terrified.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of DRYAD is its Y; replacing it with E gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Great fear or terror is a direct synonym, as in waiting with mounting apprehension.

clue.text: Notes about Athenian character held by 27

indicators.note: about means the two notes stand around the Greek letter

parts.note: TE and RE are two notes of the sol-fa scale
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a character an Athenian would write

explanation.surface: Musical notes surround a Greek letter, owned by whoever fills clue 27.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is INCUMBENT, the holder of a church living; what such a holder enjoys is the period of holding office. 'Notes' supplies two sol-fa notes, which 'about' sets either side of the Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: What an office-holder has is the right of possessing the post for a term, a synonym of that holding.

clue.text: Playwright, good at picking a quarrel?

definitions.meaning: John ..., Jacobean dramatist who collaborated with Beaumont and Shakespeare
a quarrel is a crossbow bolt, and an arrow-maker is skilled at choosing and fletching arrows

explanation.surface: A dramatist who is something of a troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picking a quarrel' suggests starting a row; a quarrel is also a square-headed crossbow bolt, and an arrow-maker's trade name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: John Fletcher was an English dramatist; an arrow-maker who fits feathers to shafts bears this trade name.

clue.text: Limit a debate on capital punishment

definitions.meaning: in Parliament, to impose a timetable cutting short discussion of a bill
the beheading machine of the French Revolution

explanation.surface: Cut short discussion about the death penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary procedure for curtailing discussion; also the French blade device for beheading.

clue.text: Railwaymen in county finally uncouple the tender

indicators.note: in means the union's letters sit inside the county abbreviation

parts.note: Staffs is the abbreviation for Staffordshire, an English county
the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of the word uncouple is used

explanation.surface: Rail workers in the shires end up detaching the coal wagon behind the engine.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'tender' is the coal truck behind a locomotive; here it is one who tends patients. NUR goes into STAFFS (Staffordshire, an English county), then E ends 'uncouple'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender is one who looks after others, and this hospital rank is a registered carer on a ward.

clue.text: Reform Lancaster inherited from his forebears

indicators.note: reform means the letters of the place name are re-formed in a new order

explanation.surface: A Lancashire city remade according to family tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reform' rearranges LANCASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to or handed down from one's line of descent, an adjective about family heritage.

clue.text: On which the speaker almost made a bloomer

indicators.note: almost means the flower's name loses its last letter

parts.note: a daisy is a flower, something that blooms

explanation.surface: Someone addressing a meeting nearly put their foot in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made a bloomer' looks like making a blunder; a bloomer is a flower, DAISY, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised platform for a lecturer or speaker to stand on at the front of a hall.

clue.text: Spanish leaders properly regarded as full of life

parts.note: SP are the leading letters of Spanish, its usual abbreviation Sp.
rightly means properly or correctly

explanation.surface: Heads of Spain are rightly considered vigorous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanish leaders' are the two leading letters of Spanish, SP, also its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively and energetic, especially of an older person, a synonym of spry.

clue.text: Sir Toby might hang like an icicle on his beard, Fabian warned

definitions.text: Sir Toby might hang like an icicle on his beard, Fabian warned

parts.words: Sir Toby might hang like an icicle on his beard, Fabian warned
parts.note: points to Fabian's line in Twelfth Night about hanging like an icicle on the beard of a native of the Netherlands

explanation.surface: A warning from a Shakespeare character that a knight could end up frozen in someone's whiskers.
explanation.walkthrough: In Twelfth Night Act 3, Fabian tells the knight he will 'hang like an icicle on a Dutchman's beard'; the clue gives the speaker as Sir Toby's companion, not Toby himself.
explanation.definitionFit: The man from the Netherlands whose frozen beard Fabian invokes in Shakespeare's comedy.

clue.text: Part of a court which may be dry

definitions.meaning: the enclosure in a criminal courtroom where the accused stands
a dry harbour basin, pumped out so ships can be repaired

explanation.surface: Some area of a courtroom that might be parched.
explanation.definitionFit: The defendant's enclosure in a courtroom; also a harbour basin that can be drained for ship repairs.

clue.text: An old ruler represented, as a versatile person

indicators.note: represented means the letters of the phrase are shown again in a new form

explanation.surface: A former monarch is portrayed as a jack of all trades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Represented' rearranges AN OLD RULER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skilled in many fields, especially a cricketer who both bats and bowls, is called this.

clue.text: Sundry underwater explorers

definitions.meaning: various or several, an old adjective
people who swim beneath the surface, like scuba enthusiasts

explanation.surface: Assorted scuba enthusiasts.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adjective meaning various or several; also people who swim submerged.

clue.text: Convict admitting a prison is impregnable

indicators.note: admitting means the convict's letters let the other pieces inside

parts.note: con is short for convict
stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A felon lets in a jail that cannot be broken out of.
explanation.walkthrough: CON takes in A and STIR (slang for jail).
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively unbreakable or rigid, like an alibi that is solid and cannot be challenged.

clue.text: Funny bird mostly seen around the motorway

indicators.note: seen around means the shortened bird surrounds the motorway
mostly means the bird's name loses its last letter

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
the M1 is Britain's first major motorway, written as MI

explanation.surface: An amusing bird spotted hanging about near a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1, Britain's main London-to-Leeds motorway, is written with the digit as the letter I. 'Mostly' trims the bird's last letter, and 'seen around' puts what is left round the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusing, causing laughter, a direct synonym.

clue.text: On the stage as a stand-in

definitions.meaning: performing in plays as a profession
serving temporarily in another's place, as with a deputy head

explanation.surface: An understudy treading the boards.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing roles in the theatre; also temporarily filling a post, as in a deputy chairman.

clue.text: Displaying clumsiness in Oriental exercises

parts.note: E for east, the Orient
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: Clumsy at Eastern martial routines.
explanation.walkthrough: E stands for East, the Orient; PT is physical training.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward or lacking skill, a synonym for clumsy and incompetent.

clue.text: Amount of money covering copyright in a dirty film

indicators.note: covering means the money word goes around the copyright letter

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money
C is the symbol for copyright

explanation.surface: Cash invested in rights to a pornographic movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty film' suggests a seedy movie; here it is a layer of grime. SUM covers C.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer of froth or impurities floating on a liquid's surface.

clue.text: Join horse in lake

indicators.note: in means the horse's letter goes inside the word for lake

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pond
gee, as in gee-gee, a child's word for horse, shortened to G

explanation.surface: A horse is put in among the waters of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: G (from gee-gee, a horse) sits in MERE.
explanation.definitionFit: To combine or blend together, as two companies do when amalgamating, a synonym.

clue.text: It's obligatory for the holder of a benefice

definitions.meaning: binding as a duty, as in a task resting upon someone
a vicar or rector holding a church living

explanation.surface: A rule that a church living must have a vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: Binding as a duty upon someone; also a clergyman who holds a parish living, or anyone in office.

clue.text: Poor souls come to the theatre

indicators.note: poor means the letters are in a bad, disordered state and so rearranged

explanation.surface: Wretched folk come along to watch a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges SOULS COME.
explanation.definitionFit: The great amphitheatre of ancient Rome, and also the name of the London Coliseum opera house, a famous venue.

clue.text: Spruce as a couple of squares in an American city

indicators.note: in means the other letters go inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York
a T-square is a draughtsman's square, so two of them are TT

explanation.surface: Neat as a pair of blocks laid out in a US city.
explanation.walkthrough: A T-square is a draughtsman's ruling tool, so two squares are two Ts; with A they go inside the New York abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce and dapper both describe someone smart and neat in appearance.
